analysis.title: Robinhood Markets Inc. (HOOD): Modest core beat, and constructive platform growth, although slightly weaker transaction revenue outlook
key_insights: HOOD reported 3Q26 EPS of 51¢ vs GSe 54¢ and Visible Alpha consensus 55¢. Core adjusted EPS (ex SBC, normalized tax rate, ex venture gains/losses) was 63¢ vs GSe 62¢ and Street 61¢. GS expects a mixed response to the print.
Core operating income beat the Street by 5%, driven by total expenses 5% lower than the Street.
October MTD net deposits were over $13bn, including a one-time ~$6bn Trump account gift from the Dell Family Foundation. HOOD is tracking meaningfully above its 20% annual net new assets target.
October MTD event contract volumes are tracking ~10% above 3Q26 levels, implying ~9% sequential growth.
Average earning assets grew 10% QoQ, driven by 21% stronger segregated cash balances and 9% stronger card balances.

International expansion continued, with regulatory approvals to operate in Dubai and Singapore. The product roadmap includes early traction in DeFi perpetuals and P2P payments for both HOOD app and non-HOOD app users.

Transaction revenue outlook is modestly weaker. Take rates fell across products in 3Q26, with modest further QTD declines in 4Q26. October to date equity, options and crypto volumes are tracking ~5% below 3Q26 ADVs, with the deceleration most visible in crypto.
3Q26 net revenue of $1.4bn was in line with consensus and up 12% YoY. Other revenue was 3% higher and NII 2% lower than consensus.

Transaction-based revenue of $867mn rose 19% YoY. Crypto and options revenue were 9% and 3% above consensus, while equities and other transaction revenue were 8% and 5% below. Crypto included ~$26mn from Robinhood Chain transaction revenue, which has moderated meaningfully since an elevated September.

NII of $415mn was 2% below consensus and down 9% YoY, on a 6bps NIM miss partly offset by 1% higher average earning assets. The miss came mainly from securities lending and segregated cash interest income, which were ~255% and 15% below consensus.

Adjusted operating expenses ex SBC of $659mn were 8% below GSe and 3% below consensus. Management lowered the top end of the 2026 adjusted opex outlook by $25mn to $2.675-2.75bn, about 1% below consensus at the midpoint.
GS cuts 2026E/27E/28E net revenue by 2%/2%/1% and transaction-based revenue by 3%/4%/3%. NII estimates rise 1%/3%/3% on higher 3Q26 average earning assets from credit card growth.
GS cuts 2026E/27E/28E adjusted pre-tax margins by 0.7pp/0.8pp/0.6pp to 52.3%/55.9%/57.3%, and adjusted EPS by 4%/4%/2%.

GS lowers its Q5-Q8 P/E target multiple by 5.0x to 35.0x from 40.0x, citing lower market multiples. The 12-month price target falls 12% to $128 from $145. Rating remains Buy, with the stock at $94.56 (35.4% upside).

market_movers.rationale: PT cut to $128 from $145 on lower estimates and a lower target P/E multiple of 35.0x. Buy rating maintained after a modest core beat and a softer transaction revenue outlook.

3Q26 core adjusted EPS 63¢ (ex SBC, normalized tax rate, adjusted for estimated venture portfolio gains/losses) vs GSe 62¢ and Street 61¢.
3Q26 net revenue $1.4bn, in line with consensus, up 12% YoY. Transaction-based revenue $867mn, up 19% YoY. NII $415mn, 2% below consensus, down 9% YoY.
3Q26 adjusted operating expenses ex SBC were $659mn, 8% below GSe and 3% below consensus.
2026 adjusted operating expense guidance lowered to $2.675-2.75bn, about 1% below consensus at the midpoint.
crypto_views: Crypto revenue was 9% above consensus in 3Q26, including ~$26mn from Robinhood Chain transaction revenue, which has moderated meaningfully since an elevated September.

September crypto notional volume was $21.4bn (+22% MoM), with $8.9bn from the Robinhood App and $12.5bn from Bitstamp. October to date crypto volumes are tracking ~5% below the 3Q26 run rate, the most pronounced slowdown among product lines.
HOOD is seeing early traction in DeFi perpetuals.
risk_factors: Lower interest rates impacting the NII growth trajectory.
Weaker cross-sell of new products to the user base at lower margins.
